name: object 3
text:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely integrated into healthcare SaaS platforms for documentation, triage, summarization, and clinical support.
These systems are vulnerable to semantic adversarial attacks such as prompt injection and PHI extraction.
Traditional cybersecurity mechanisms cannot detect natural language-based manipulation.
We propose a hybrid, risk-aware, healthcare-specific security framework for real-time LLM protection.

name: object 3
text:
Healthcare LLM systems process sensitive data including electronic health records and patient interactions.
Prompt injection attacks exploit contextual reasoning by embedding malicious instructions within legitimate queries.
Such attacks can override policies and extract confidential patient information.
There is a need for domain-aware, adaptive, and explainable LLM guardrails.

text:
The existing LLM security approaches mainly focus on individual attacks and fixed mechanisms, lacking a unified, adaptive, and risk-aware framework for real-time healthcare LLM security.

 Fragmented Security: Individual threats are addressed separately. 
 Limited Adaptability: Static rules cannot adjust to changing threats. 
 Lack of Risk Scoring: Mostly binary safe/unsafe decisions. 
 Limited Real-Time Monitoring: Insufficient continuous monitoring. 
 Detection–Response Gap: Limited automatic blocking or mitigation. 
 Limited ML/DL Integration: Need to combine AI models with rule-based security. 
 Healthcare Security Gap: Limited protection of sensitive healthcare information.

2. To implement adaptive behavioral anomaly detection for identifying abnormal user interaction patterns and risk escalation.

3. To develop a formal weighted risk aggregation model with integrated Explainable AI mechanisms for transparent decision-making.

name: object 2
text:
1. Core System Components
Transformer Classifier – A healthcare-trained DistilBERT model used for multi-class prompt injection and jailbreak detection.
Semantic Similarity Engine – Uses Sentence-BERT embeddings and cosine similarity to detect paraphrased adversarial prompts.
Healthcare Rule Engine – Applies regex-based and policy-based rules to detect direct privacy violations and override attempts.
PHI Detection Module – Uses spaCy NER and pattern matching to identify sensitive healthcare information such as names, IDs, and medical records.
Behavioral Anomaly Engine – Models user interaction patterns and detects abnormal risk escalation or unusual prompt behavior.
Explainability Module – Uses SHAP analysis to provide transparent reasoning behind risk decisions.
Risk Aggregator & Decision Engine – Combines all module outputs using a weighted mathematical formula to generate a final risk score and allow/flag/block decision.

text:
Security prompt corpus: 5 labels — safe, malicious, jailbreak, PHI and suspicious.

Split used for data preparation: 11,463 training / 2,369 validation / 2,370 test prompts.

Sources: MPIB, MedQuAD, PubMedQA and controlled synthetic prompts for PHI, jailbreak and general healthcare cases.

Quality checks: no missing core fields after validation; attack severity and source distribution were profiled.

Retrieval knowledge base: 15,979 healthcare documents and FAISS vectors.

name: object 3
text:
Training run: DistilBERT-base-uncased, 5 classes, max length 256, 4 epochs, batch size 16 and learning rate 2e-5.

Held-out security test: 2,306 samples; accuracy 93.89%; macro precision 86.40%; macro recall 87.20%; macro F1 86.73%.

Best validation macro F1: 86.21%; best validation accuracy: 93.28%.

FAISS retrieval: Top-1 61%; Top-3 85%; Top-5 93% across 100 evaluation queries.

Review insight: suspicious-class F1 is 49.50%, so it is the priority for data enrichment and threshold tuning.

name: object 3
text:
1. Normalize and tokenize each prompt, then run detection before forwarding to the downstream LLM.

2. Classifier estimates threat intent; SentenceTransformer embeddings calculate cosine similarity against attack patterns.

3. Transformer NER plus regex rules detect PHI/PII and redact matched spans while retaining offsets.

4. Risk aggregation: R = 0.50T + 0.30H + 0.20S, where T = classifier threat, H = PHI risk and S = similarity risk.

5. Enforcement: Block at risk ≥75 or high-confidence injection; mask PHI; quarantine risk ≥45; otherwise allow and audit.

The proposed hybrid adaptive risk-aware framework improves detection accuracy, enhances explainability, and provides real-time risk-based decision-making, making healthcare AI systems more secure and reliable.
